The Level Chart of a Filter's Joint Fit

Source: R/structural.R
joint_level_chart.Rd

The change of coordinates under which statmod_fit_joint() searches a free level: the level \(\omega\) of a score-driven term is replaced by \(L = \omega / \prod_k (1 - r_k)\), the level around which the predictor fluctuates, \(r_k\) being the partial autocorrelations that carry the persistence (by the Durbin-Levinson recursion, \(1 - \sum_k \phi_k = \prod_k (1 - r_k)\)). The other coordinates are unchanged.

Usage

joint_level_chart(spec, jp)

Arguments

spec

A StatmodSpec().

jp

The joint pieces, as statmod_joint_pieces() returns them.

Value

NULL, or a list of the functions to (chart to the term's coordinates), from, grad and hess.

Details

The chart applies where the level is one free coordinate on the identity link and every persistence is a free scalar partial autocorrelation; in any other case the result is NULL and the fit runs on the term's own coordinates. With \(\omega = L P(\rho)\), the gradient is \(J^\top g\) and the Hessian \(J^\top H J + g_\omega \nabla^2 \omega\), \(J\) the Jacobian of the map.
